speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin narrowing this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and have they progressively worsened over time? Additionally, do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for clarifying; since the symptoms are recent and asymmetric with prominent ataxia, have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, hearing, or balance issues like vertigo? Also, do you have any history of autoimmune disorders or recent infections?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain axial and coronal slices

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast findings indicate lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). I suspect this is due to severe immunosuppression or an underlying HIV infection; are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications or do you have a known history of HIV?
